title: Backgrounds & Borders
summary: Backgrounds and borders add color, images, and edges to an element.

subtopics.title: Main property
subtopics.explanation: `background-color` paints the area behind an element’s content and padding. For example, a pale background can make a help panel easy to distinguish. It is like putting colored paper behind a note. Check that text still has enough contrast, and remember that backgrounds may be disabled in some print settings. For example, give a warning panel a background and a text label so the state is not color-only.

subtopics.title: What it changes
subtopics.explanation: `background-image` can show a picture, pattern, or gradient behind content. A gradient is a gradual color transition. It is like printing a faint texture on paper. Keep text readable over it, and provide the same meaning in text if the image communicates information. Large decorative images can also increase download time. For example, use a gradient only if text remains readable over every part of it.

subtopics.title: Another useful choice
subtopics.explanation: `border` draws a line around an element, with a width, style, and color. For example, `border: 1px solid #bbb` gives a subtle outline. It is like the edge of a card. Use borders to clarify grouping or interaction states, and do not rely on color alone to show that a field has an error. For example, a border can distinguish an input that has keyboard focus.

subtopics.title: Common behavior
subtopics.explanation: `border-radius` rounds the corners of a box. A small radius can soften a card; a fully rounded value can make a pill-shaped button. It is like rounding the corners of a paper ticket. Keep the shape consistent across related controls so users can recognize which elements belong together. For example, a border radius changes shape without changing the content’s meaning.

subtopics.title: Good practice
subtopics.explanation: Choose backgrounds and borders based on what the component needs to communicate. A form error needs text and a visible state; a decorative hero may use an image. This is like choosing a frame only when it helps people notice the picture. Test colors in light and dark themes, at high zoom, and when styles are printed. For example, provide a solid fallback color when a background image fails to load.

foundations.overview: Backgrounds and borders help separate and decorate parts of a page. A background sits behind an element’s content; a border draws an edge around its box. Think of a card as paper on a desk: the background is the paper color, and the border is its outline. Use these styles to support hierarchy and readability, not to replace meaningful text or labels.
foundations.whyItMatters: Backgrounds and borders make visual grouping and interaction states easier to recognize. Contrast, fallback behavior, and non-color cues keep those styles usable in more situations.
foundations.browserPerspective: During painting, the browser fills the background layers from back (color) to front (last-to-first image), then strokes the border, clipping backgrounds to the border-radius. Outline is painted separately and isn't part of the box model's size calculation.
foundations.realWorldUsage: Cards with a subtle background and 1px border and rounded corners; hero sections with an image plus a dark gradient overlay; buttons with background-color and hover changes; and accessible focus rings via outline.
foundations.businessImpact: Polished, consistent surfaces improve perceived quality and trust, while visible focus styles keep products accessible and compliant.
foundations.engineeringImpact: Knowing that border needs a style, that backgrounds clip to border-radius, and that outline doesn't shift layout eliminates a whole class of confusing visual bugs.
foundations.performanceImpact: CSS gradients and colors are cheap; large background images cost bandwidth and can hurt rendering, so optimize and size them (and prefer cover/contain over huge tiled images).
commonUseCases: Hero sections: an image with a gradient overlay via multiple backgrounds
Buttons: background-color with hover/active state changes

commonMisconceptions.myth: Setting border-width and border-color shows a border.
commonMisconceptions.reality: A border is invisible until border-style is set; without a style there's nothing to draw.
outline is drawn outside the box, takes no layout space, and is meant for focus; border is part of the box model and affects size and layout.

commonMisconceptions.myth: A background image is a good place for essential instructions.
commonMisconceptions.reality: Essential information should remain available as text and not depend on a decorative image.

commonMisconceptions.myth: A border color alone makes an error accessible.
commonMisconceptions.reality: Pair color with clear text or another visible indicator for the error state.

visualExplorer.title: How a box gets decorated
visualExplorer.caption: Step through how backgrounds layer behind content and how borders, radius, and outline are drawn around the box.

steps.title: Fill the background color
steps.description: background-color paints the box (padding box) behind the content.

steps.title: Paint background images
steps.description: background-image layers sit above the color; with multiple, the first listed is on top.

steps.title: Position and size the image
steps.description: background-repeat, position, and size (cover/contain) control how the image is placed and scaled.

steps.title: Draw the border
steps.description: border-style makes the border visible; width and color complete it. Border adds to size unless box-sizing: border-box.

steps.title: Round the corners
steps.description: border-radius rounds the box and clips the background to match.

steps.title: Add the focus outline
steps.description: outline is drawn outside the border, takes no layout space, and signals keyboard focus.

codeLab.title: Style a pill button
codeLab.instructions: Give .btn a blue background-color, white text, no visible border but a fully rounded shape with border-radius. Add a focus outline for accessibility. Fill the TODOs.
codeLab.expectedOutput: A rounded blue pill button with white text and a visible focus ring when tabbed to.
hints: border-radius: 999px (a very large value) makes a pill shape.
Use outline (not border) for the focus ring so it doesn't shift layout.

keyTakeaways: `background-color` paints the area behind an element’s content and padding.
`background-image` can show a picture, pattern, or gradient behind content.
`border` draws a line around an element, with a width, style, and color.
`border-radius` rounds the corners of a box.
Choose backgrounds and borders based on what the component needs to communicate.
